english: to submit/file (an application), to register a request
usage: Often used at a counter (창구) — you hand in paperwork and it gets 'received/registered.'
접수 is also a noun on signs: 접수처 (reception desk), 접수 시간 (intake hours).
examples: 신청서는 1층에서 접수해 주세요.
Please submit the application form on the first floor.
Typical instruction at a 주민센터 or office.
오늘까지 접수해야 처리가 가능해요.
It has to be filed by today for it to be processed.
접수 (filing) is step one; 처리 (processing) comes after.
온라인으로도 접수할 수 있나요?
Can I also file it online?
Useful question at any government or company desk.
nuance: 접수하다 means to formally hand in or lodge something so it enters the system — an application, complaint, or request. From the staff's side it means 'to receive/accept' the submission, so on signs 접수 is the intake counter. It feels more bureaucratic than the everyday 내다 ('to hand in').
mistakes: Don't confuse 접수하다 (file/lodge a request) with 접속하다 (to log in / connect online) — they look similar but are unrelated.

english: to fill out/write up (a form or document)
usage: to fill out an application form
The default verb for completing any form, contract, or report.
빠짐없이 = 'leaving nothing out,' a common phrase on forms.
examples: 이 칸은 한글로 작성해 주세요.
Please fill in this box in Korean.
칸 = a box/field on a form.
계약서를 작성하기 전에 꼼꼼히 읽어 보세요.
Read it carefully before filling out the contract.
계약서 = contract; very relevant for housing/jobs.
보고서는 내일까지 작성해야 해요.
I have to write up the report by tomorrow.
Common office deadline phrasing.
nuance: 작성하다 is the standard, slightly formal verb for filling out or composing a structured document — forms, contracts, reports, emails. Use it instead of 쓰다 ('to write') whenever there's a template or official format to complete. You'll hear it constantly at offices and at work.
mistakes: For a quick handwritten note use 쓰다; 작성하다 implies an official form or document, so '메모를 작성하다' can sound overly stiff for a casual note.

english: to be issued / to get issued (a document or card)
usage: Used for any official document you receive: 등본, 증명서, 카드, 비자.
Add 재- for replacing a lost card or document.
examples: 외국인등록증을 발급받으려면 어디로 가야 해요?
Where do I go to get my alien registration card issued?
Key task for residents at 출입국 (immigration).
주민등록등본은 무인발급기에서도 발급받을 수 있어요.
You can also get a resident registration copy from a self-service kiosk.
무인발급기 = unmanned issuing machine.
체크카드를 잃어버려서 재발급받았어요.
I lost my debit card so I got it reissued.
Shows the very common 재발급받다; 체크카드 = debit card.
nuance: 발급받다 is from your side — you receive/obtain an officially issued document. The office's side uses 발급하다 ('to issue'). For residents this verb is everywhere: ID cards, bank cards, certificates, visas. The opposite action of getting one for the first time vs. again is 발급받다 vs. 재발급받다.
mistakes: Don't say 발급하다 about yourself — that's what the issuing office does. You 발급받다 (receive issuance).

usage: Used for memberships, courses, devices, and official registration.
등록 as a noun appears on signs: 등록증 (registration certificate), 등록 마감.
examples: 지문을 등록해야 출입할 수 있어요.
You have to register your fingerprint to enter.
Common in offices/gyms with biometric access.
수강 신청은 다음 주에 등록하면 돼요.
You can register for the course next week.
수강 신청 = course registration.
계좌를 자동이체로 등록했어요.
I registered my account for automatic transfer.
자동이체 = auto-debit; a practical banking task.
nuance: 등록하다 means to officially enter something into a system — yourself as a member, a class enrollment, a device, or biometric data. It's broader than 가입하다 ('to join/subscribe'), which is mainly for memberships and services. Think 'put on the register/list.'
mistakes: 등록하다 vs 가입하다: 가입하다 is specifically joining a service/club/insurance; 등록하다 is registering data or enrolling. Don't use 등록하다 for 'subscribe to a service.'

usage: The crucial use for residents: visa, stay, contract, deadline.
Used for lease renewals and job contracts.
examples: 체류 기간을 연장하러 출입국에 가야 해요.
I have to go to immigration to extend my period of stay.
체류 기간 = period of stay; core resident vocabulary.
도서관 책 대출을 한 번 더 연장할 수 있어요.
You can extend the library book loan one more time.
대출 = loan/borrowing.
마감을 이틀만 연장해 주시면 안 될까요?
Could you possibly extend the deadline by just two days?
Polite workplace request.
nuance: 연장하다 means to make a time period longer — a visa, contract, loan, deadline, or operating hours. For renewing something that expires, Koreans often say 연장하다 (extend) or 갱신하다 (renew); 연장 stresses 'more time,' 갱신 stresses 'issuing a new term.' For visas you'll hear both, but 연장 is the everyday word.
mistakes: Don't confuse 연장 (extend a duration) with 연락 (contact). And for renewing an ID/license, 갱신하다 is often the official term, though 연장하다 is widely understood.

english: to pay (a bill/tax/fee to an institution)
usage: Formal verb for paying official dues: taxes, fees, insurance, fines.
납부 appears on bills: 납부 마감일, 미납 (unpaid/overdue).
examples: 관리비는 매달 25일까지 납부해야 해요.
Maintenance fees must be paid by the 25th each month.
관리비 = building maintenance fee; standard for apartment renters.
과태료를 기한 안에 납부하면 할인돼요.
If you pay the fine within the deadline, you get a discount.
과태료 = administrative fine; early payment often discounted.
건강보험료를 자동이체로 납부하고 있어요.
I pay my health insurance premium by auto-debit.
건강보험료 = health insurance premium.
nuance: 납부하다 is the formal verb for paying money owed to an institution — taxes, public utilities, insurance premiums, fines, tuition. It's not used for everyday shopping; for that you use 내다 ('pay') or just 결제하다 ('settle/pay by card'). On official bills and notices you'll always see 납부, not 지불.
mistakes: Don't use 납부하다 when buying things at a store — use 결제하다 or 계산하다. 납부하다 is specifically for dues/bills to an authority.

english: to process / to handle / to deal with
usage: Covers processing paperwork, requests, and getting things done.
Status phrase on applications and tickets: 처리 완료 = done.
examples: 신청서가 접수되면 3일 안에 처리됩니다.
Once the application is received, it is processed within 3 days.
Shows the passive 처리되다 used in official notices.
이 문제는 제가 처리할게요.
I'll handle this issue.
Reassuring phrase at work.
환불 처리는 어디서 하나요?
Where do I get the refund processed?
환불 처리 = refund processing.
nuance: 처리하다 is a workhorse verb meaning to process, handle, or take care of a task, request, or problem. The passive 처리되다 ('be processed') is everywhere on official status messages. It's neutral and professional — perfect for both office work and dealing with paperwork.
mistakes: Learners overuse 하다 alone; saying 'I'll do this issue' is wrong. Use 처리하다 to mean 'handle/take care of' a matter.

usage: Formal 'ask' for businesses, offices, customer service.
문의 as a noun on signs: 문의처 (contact for inquiries), 문의 전화.
examples: 자세한 사항은 고객센터로 문의해 주세요.
For details, please inquire with the customer center.
고객센터 = customer service; standard closing line.
비자 관련해서 출입국에 문의했어요.
I inquired with immigration about visa matters.
Very relevant resident situation.
가격은 매장에 직접 문의하시면 됩니다.
For the price, you can inquire directly at the store.
Polite 하시면 됩니다 = 'you may ~.'
nuance: 문의하다 is the formal, polite verb for making an inquiry to a business or institution — by phone, email, or in person. It's more official than 물어보다 ('to ask'), which you'd use with friends or in casual situations. You'll see 문의 on every company's contact page.
mistakes: Use 물어보다 for asking a friend a question; 문의하다 sounds too formal between individuals and is meant for organizations/services.

english: to report / to declare / to notify (officially)
usage: Required after moving — registering your new address at the 주민센터.
Used for lost cards/phones/passports; also 도난 신고 (theft report).
examples: 이사하면 14일 안에 전입신고를 해야 해요.
After moving you must file a move-in report within 14 days.
전입신고 = move-in registration; a legal requirement.
카드를 잃어버려서 바로 분실 신고했어요.
I lost my card so I reported it lost right away.
Practical, urgent action.
문제가 생기면 112에 신고하세요.
If there's a problem, report it to 112.
112 = police emergency line in Korea.
nuance: 신고하다 means to officially report or declare something to an authority — a move, a loss, an emergency, taxes (세금 신고), or wrongdoing. It always points toward a government office or official channel, unlike 알리다 ('to inform') which is general. 전입신고 is one of the first things every newcomer must do.
mistakes: Don't confuse 신고하다 (report to authorities) with 신청하다 (apply for). 신고 = notify/declare; 신청 = request/apply.

usage: Standard verb for signing official documents.
The exact phrase staff say when handing you a pen.
examples: 내용을 확인하고 여기에 서명해 주세요.
Please check the contents and sign here.
확인하고 = after confirming; common at counters.
계약서에 서명하기 전에 다시 한번 읽어 봤어요.
I read the contract once more before signing it.
Smart habit for housing/job contracts.
전자 서명도 인정되나요?
Is an electronic signature also accepted?
전자 서명 = e-signature; increasingly common.
nuance: 서명하다 means to sign your name on a document. Note that Korea traditionally uses a personal stamp called 도장 (or the registered 인감) on many official papers, so you may be asked for a 서명 (signature) or a 도장 instead. In daily life both are widely accepted, but some legal documents still prefer the stamp.
mistakes: 서명하다 is signing your name; don't confuse it with 사인하다 (a casual loanword also meaning 'to sign,' common in speech). For formal documents, 서명 is the proper term.

usage: The standard office/admin verb for printing files.
to print in black and white
컬러 출력 = color printing; common copy-shop request.
examples: 등본을 출력해서 가져오세요.
Print out the registration copy and bring it.
등본 = official certified copy; frequent admin request.
편의점에서도 서류를 출력할 수 있어요.
You can print documents at convenience stores too.
Korean convenience stores have self-print kiosks.
파일을 PDF로 저장하고 출력했어요.
I saved the file as PDF and printed it.
Everyday office workflow.
nuance: 출력하다 is the formal/technical word for printing from a computer, common in offices and on kiosks. In casual speech people also say 프린트하다 ('to print'). 출력 literally means 'output,' so it can also refer to computer output more broadly, but in daily admin life it almost always means 'print out.'
mistakes: Don't confuse 출력하다 (print/output) with 입력하다 (input/type in). 출력 = out, 입력 = in.

english: to sign up / to join / to enroll in (a service or plan)
usage: Takes the particle 에: you join 'into' a service or plan.
가입 as a noun is the 'Sign Up' button everywhere online.
examples: 휴대폰 요금제에 새로 가입했어요.
I just signed up for a new phone plan.
요금제 = phone plan; a first-week task for residents.
이 앱은 가입하지 않아도 쓸 수 있어요?
Can I use this app without signing up?
Useful question to avoid making an account.
건강보험에 가입하려면 어떤 서류가 필요해요?
What documents do I need to enroll in health insurance?
건강보험 = national health insurance.
nuance: 가입하다 means to join or sign up for a service, plan, club, or insurance, and it takes the particle 에 (보험에 가입하다). Compare 등록하다 ('register/enroll data') and 신청하다 ('apply/request'): 가입하다 specifically means becoming a member or subscriber. 회원 가입 is the universal 'Sign Up' on Korean apps and sites.
mistakes: Use 에, not 을/를: it's 보험에 가입하다, not 보험을 가입하다. The thing you join takes 에.
